record.field: Sets up campaigns, templates, contacts and call teams when you ask. Everything it makes is a draft.
Its tools, the yes or no step before it makes anything, and the rule that everything stays a draft are fixed in code. Changing the wording here cannot switch them off.
Answers staff questions about candidates, callbacks, CVs and jobs. It only looks things up.
What it can look up is fixed in code: first names and lists only, never a surname, a phone number or an ID number.
Sums up a conversation, reads the mood and suggests a reply for the agent to send.
Runs on a timer, on conversations with new messages
The screen reads its answer by the three labels SUMMARY, SENTIMENT and SUGGESTED_REPLY. Keep them in the wording or the answer cannot be read.
Writes up a recorded call: a summary, the mood and the outcome.
Runs after a recorded call has been typed out
The transcript is added after this wording. The answer is read as JSON with summary, sentiment and disposition: keep those three names.
Reads an uploaded CV into the standard CV form. The candidate is asked to check it.
Runs on a timer, on newly uploaded CVs
The CV form it fills in, and the limit of five jobs and five schools or courses, are fixed in code.
Puts each new job post under the right occupation. Staff can change it; theirs is kept.
Runs on a timer, on job posts with no occupation
The list of occupation codes is added after this wording. The cost shown also covers sorting CVs, which has its own wording in code.
